Rule: All given cells contain the same solid square, so the missing cell must also be a solid square.
All visible matrix cells contain the same circle enclosing a plus sign, so the missing cell matches them.
The triangle is reflected horizontally from left to right, while the top and bottom rows match.
The missing quarter rotates by reflection: rightward swaps left/right and downward swaps top/bottom, so the final gap is at the top-left.
The bottom row is the vertical reflection of the top row, so B's lower-left block becomes an upper-left block.
Reflect horizontally across the top row and vertically plus change from filled to outline down the left column.
The figure in the bottom row repeats the corresponding figure directly above it, so the missing cell must match B.
Across each row, the outlined shape becomes filled while retaining its form.
The diamond is removed from left to right, while the outer shape changes from heart to octagon from top to bottom.
Both moving right and moving down removes two concentric circles and reduces the overall size; thus the missing cell has one small circle.
Each row increases the number of nested squares by one: 1, then 2, then 3.
The outlined square increases by one fixed size step from left to right and from top to bottom, while the central black square remains constant.
The number of diamonds increases by a constant factor across rows and columns: 1-2-3, 2-4-6, and 3-6-9.
Each cell combines the column’s number of horizontally arranged circles (1, 2, 3) with the row’s number of vertically arranged circles (1, 2, 3), so the missing cell needs a 3-by-3 arrangement.
Dots are cumulatively added across columns (right then lower-right) and down rows (left then lower-left), while the top dot remains constant.
Rectangle width increases across columns while height increases down rows.
The circle moves through the eight compass positions around the diamond in reading order, with the center cell representing overlap so the diamond is hidden.
Each inner cell overlays its column-header and row-header square patterns, with overlapping black squares becoming outlines.
Each row shows a pair of identical shapes facing inward, overlapping, then facing outward; the third row uses stars.
Each row sets the vertical relation (single, touching, separated) and each column sets the horizontal relation (single, touching, separated), combined in each cell.
Each step right adds one diamond along the bottom row from left to center, while each step down removes the highest diamond in the right-hand vertical column.
Across columns the black area expands leftward along the top row, and down rows it expands upward along the left column, leaving the lower-right 2×2 grid.
Each row contains the same shape repeated across all three columns.
Each row and column contains one filled circle, one filled diamond, and one filled triangle.
Each row and column cycles through the three figure sets: circle alone, triangle-plus-circle, and triangle-plus-circle-plus-square.
Rows determine the inner symbol (plus, star, heart), while columns determine the enclosing outline (circle, diamond, square).
Each row keeps the same central polygon, while the columns change its surrounding/inner marking from an enclosing outline circle to a white circular cutout to two external black dots.
Each row cyclically shifts the three symbols (circle, plus, triangle), while the number of nested square outlines decreases from three to two to one down the rows.
Each row and column cycles the inner shapes (plus, square, heart) and the outer surrounds (dots, circle, matching outline), so the missing cell is a square with four dots.
Each row and column cycles through square, diamond, and circle, while the display style cycles through filled alone, outline alone, and filled-inside-outline.
Both the outer shapes and bar patterns shift cyclically across rows and columns, requiring an octagon with a vertical bar.

The central shapes cycle square→diamond→circle across rows and columns, while the surrounding pattern cycles detached cardinal squares→diagonal arms→cardinal arms; therefore the missing cell is a square with diagonal arms.
The three star styles cycle leftward across each row and downward: solid star, solid star with white center, outlined star with black center.
Each row and column cycles through square, triangle, and star shapes, while the counts cycle through 3, 4, and 5.
Each third cell is the combination of the first two cells in its row, and likewise the bottom cell combines the top and middle cells in its column.
Each third cell overlays the figures in the first two cells; the bottom row and right column therefore combine all four basic figures.
The third figure in each row/column is the superposition of the first two, with overlapping diamonds merged.
The figures combine by superimposing the two simpler shapes in each row and column.
In each row, the third figure is formed by removing the elements common to the first two, leaving their non-common components; thus the last cell contains only the outer square.
Each row and column combines two independent features in the middle cell, with the missing cell requiring only the diamond feature.
Each third cell is the XOR of the first two: shared elements cancel and nonshared elements remain.
Each third figure is the exclusive-or combination of the first two: shared lines cancel and nonshared lines remain.
In each row and column, the third panel combines the top shape from the first panel with the bottom shape from the second panel.
The third figure in each row is the overlap/common part of the directional extensions in the first two figures; thus the bottom row leaves only the central square.
The third figure retains the black regions shared by the first two figures (with the central overlap shifted inward in the middle row).
Treat upward triangles as +1 and downward triangles as -1; in each row and column the third/bottom cell is the algebraic sum of the first two, cancelling opposite orientations.
Across the row, triangles rotate 90° clockwise; down the column, one large triangle becomes three smaller triangles in the same orientation.
The outer alternating concentric regions are filled black while the innermost circle remains white.
Reflect vertically and change the black triangle to a striped triangle.
The shape is reflected horizontally from A to B and vertically from A to C, so the missing cell is C reflected horizontally, with stripes retained.
The number of sides increases by one from left to right and from top to bottom: 3, 4, 5, 6.
Across each row, the shape changes from circle to heart while the fill changes from vertical stripes to solid black; applying this to the second row gives a solid black heart.
Rotate each triangle and the three-triangle arrangement 90° clockwise across each row; down the first column only the triangles rotate 90° clockwise.
The shape is reflected horizontally across each row and vertically down each column.
Rotate each shape 90 degrees clockwise across the row; the octagon remains visually unchanged under this rotation.

The three figure types cycle one position across each row and down each column: A-type (nested outlines with black center), B-type (black frames with outlined center), and C-type (outlined outer frame with black inner frames).
The number of horizontal squares increases by one from left to right and from top to bottom, so the missing cell must contain five horizontal squares.
Counts increase from 1 to 3 across columns and from 1 to 3 down rows, while triangle fill alternates outline-filled-outline by column.
Each row adds one vertical line and each column adds one horizontal line, so the missing cell must contain three vertical and three horizontal lines.
Rows determine the number of vertical items (1, 2, 3), columns determine the number of horizontal items and shape type, with fill alternating by row and column.
The number of triangles equals the row number times the column number, with orientation alternating in a checkerboard pattern; thus the final cell has nine downward triangles.
Across columns black changes to diagonal hatching, while down rows black changes to opposite diagonal hatching; where both hatchings overlap, a checker pattern results.
Across each row, identical large and small shapes progress from separate, to overlapping, to concentrically nested with the dot inside the small shape.
Each row uses a different shape type and progresses from separate shapes with a dot, to overlapping shapes with the dot, to nested shapes with the dot.
Each row increases the number of shapes from 1 to 3, while columns use triangles, circles, then squares; thus the missing cell has nine squares.
Each row and column cycles through triangle, circle, and square, while the sizes cycle medium, small, and large; thus the missing figure is a medium circle.

Black quadrants accumulate from the upper-left: moving right adds the upper-right quadrant, while moving down adds the lower-left quadrant, so the final cell has all but the lower-right quadrant black.
The wedge orientation shifts one step counterclockwise across each row and down each column: right, bottom, left / bottom, left, top / left, top, right.
Each descending-right diagonal contains identical triangles, so the main diagonal must repeat the upward-pointing triangle.
Each step right or down advances the triangle through the same sequence of orientations; the missing figure is the downward-pointing triangle.
Each middle cell overlays the two paired forms from the left cell, while the right cell reverses the pair’s inward-facing cutouts to outward-facing cutouts.
Each row and column contains each shape once and each fill style once: outline, hatched, solid.
Each row and column contains one, two, and three triangles; the missing cell must have two filled right-pointing triangles.
Both the background fill (checkered, blank, striped) and the black-bar arrangement (cross, vertical, horizontal) cycle through each row and column, so the missing cell must be blank with a cross.

The triangle direction in each row is preserved from the filled triangle into the three outlined triangles, while the middle column stays upward; thus the last cell must contain three downward-pointing triangles arranged downward.
Each row and column cycles through left-side types (curved, slanted, vertical) and through 2, 3, and 4 line segments; the missing figure must have a curved side and 3 segments.
The number of symbols cycles across rows and columns: 2-3-4, 4-2-3, 3-4-2; the missing cell must contain two curved symbols.
Each third figure is the exclusive-or combination of the first two: overlapping square units cancel, while non-overlapping units remain.
In each row and column, the third panel is the union (overlay) of the filled triangles in the first two panels.
Each third cell is the intersection of the shapes in the first two cells, both across rows and down columns.
Each large figure is the combination of the two simpler component figures in its row and column; the missing component must be vertical stripes only.
The number of sides increases by two across each row and down each column: 4, 6, 8 / 6, 8, 10 / 8, 10, 12.
In each row and column, the total number of polygon sides in the third cell equals the sum of those in the first two cells; the missing cell must therefore total 16 sides.
The number of star points increases by two from left to right and from top to bottom (4, 6, 8 / 6, 8, 10 / 8, 10, 12).
The number of sides/points follows subtraction: 16−12=4, 8−4=4, and 12−4=8, so the missing figure is an 8-sided polygon.
Across the matrix, each successive cell adds one symbol, alternating X and circle, so the missing cell must contain five circles and four Xs.
The number of birds increases by one from left to right and from top to bottom.
